question: Submission description (a short paragraph)
answer: AEGIS is a reference-skeptical, corruption-shielded evaluation system. Motivated by WMT26's shift to post-edited and synthetic references, it treats the reference as just another hypothesis: a reference-based COMET-22 score and a reference-free MetricX-24 (QE-mode) score are fused with a per-segment weight derived from the reference's own estimated quality and declared type (human / postedit / pseudo / absent), falling back to pure QE where no reference exists. Before neural scoring, a deterministic Unicode-hygiene layer separates orthographic integrity from semantic quality: default-ignorable codepoints, whitespace-class substitutions, homoglyph cloaking, and Indic conjunct-breaking joiners are detected and converted into transparent point penalties (we verified XLM-R-based metrics are provably blind to several of these corruptions), and a degeneracy guard catches empty, runaway, and repetition-loop outputs. We submit predictions for every official language pair, every system, and all challenge-set items.

question: Does your system use the provided reference translations in any form? (true|false)
If your system uses reference translations, please briefly describe which types of references you use (native|postedit|pseudo) and how you use them.
answer: All reference types are used when present, but with type- and quality-dependent trust: the reference-based score's fusion weight is scaled by the reference's declared type (native > postedit > pseudo) and by a reference-free quality estimate of the reference itself, so segments with unreliable references lean on the QE branch. Items without references are scored purely reference-free.

question: Is supervised (did you fine-tune your model?) (true|false)
Model size
answer: Unbabel wmt22-comet-da (XLM-RoBERTa-large backbone, ~580M parameters) + google/metricx-24-hybrid-large-v2p6 (mT5-large backbone, ~1.2B parameters); deterministic Unicode-hygiene and degeneracy layers add no learned parameters.
